**Proposed mechanism:** ICOS (HGNC:29890) —DISRUPTS→ PI3K/Akt signaling pathway (KEGG:hsa04150); PIK3CA (HGNC:9034) —DISRUPTS→ PI3K/Akt signaling pathway (KEGG:hsa04150); PI3K/Akt signaling pathway (KEGG:hsa04150) —LEADS_TO→ Immunodeficiency (HP:0002705); PI3K/Akt signaling pathway (KEGG:hsa04150) —LEADS_TO→ Megalencephaly (HP:0000252); PI3K/Akt signaling pathway (KEGG:hsa04150) —LEADS_TO→ Capillary malformation (HP:0030177); PI3K/Akt signaling pathway (KEGG:hsa04150) —LEADS_TO→ Polymicrogyria (HP:0001311). Mutations in ICOS (for CVID) or PIK3CA (for CVID and MCAP) converge on the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway. Loss-of-function mutations in ICOS or PIK3CA disrupt this pathway, leading to immunodeficiency. Gain-of-function mutations in PIK3CA dysregulate this pathway, contributing to the characteristic phenotypes of MCAP (megalencephaly, capillary malformations, and polymicrogyria).

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in PIK3CA associated with CVID do not affect the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway, or that CVID can be fully explained by mechanisms entirely independent of PIK3CA and ICOS function.

**Why it matters:** Targeting the PI3K/Akt pathway could offer therapeutic avenues for both conditions, although the differing functional consequences of mutations (loss-of-function in CVID vs. gain-of-function in MCAP) necessitate distinct therapeutic strategies.
